S22.01.needs: A signed-in account that is allowed web search (the 'Web search' row is hidden otherwise), and a network connection
S22.01.note: In answers the citation is a teal [n] text marker; the pill chip with [n] and a title is used in Deep Research 'Sources' lists (research/ResearchSourcesAppendix.tsx).
steps: Sign in and open the Chat screen. Make sure the 'Cloud' button in the mode toggle is selected.
Tap the '+' button (its accessibility label is 'Add to chat'), turn on 'Web search', then close the sheet.
Ask: 'What are the latest headlines about renewable energy? Cite your sources.'
When the answer finishes, look for small teal bracket numbers such as [1] in the text.
Tap one [n] marker. Compare with Expected: the source should be identified (title shown) and openable through 'Open page'.
S22.01.where: Chat > '+' button > turn on 'Web search' > ask a question > teal [1], [2] markers in the answer

S22.02.needs: A signed-in account with web search on, and a network connection
S22.02.note: A phone has no hover, so the preview is a tap that shows a native alert (previewCitation in CitationChip.tsx), not a hover card. Date and snippet appear only when the source has them.
steps: Get an answer with web search on, as in S22.01, with a teal [n] marker in the text.
Tap the [n] marker.
Compare with Expected: a popup shows the source title, the site, 'Published' date when known, and a snippet when known.
Tap 'Cancel' and tap the marker again, then tap 'Open page' and check the source opens.
S22.02.where: Chat > answer with web search > tap a teal [n] marker > preview alert

S22.03.needs: A signed-in account with web search on, and a network connection
S22.03.note: While the answer is still streaming the title reads 'Sources so far'. Search steps also show a 'Searching for' card in the tool timeline (WebSearchToolCard.tsx).
steps: Get an answer with web search on, as in S22.01.
Tap the 'Sources' pill under the answer (it says 'View N sources').
Check the sheet: a query line, a 'Citations' heading for cited sources, and a 'More' heading for the rest.
Check each row shows publisher and date, the title, and a snippet when there is one.
Tap a row. Compare with Expected: the source opens in the in-app browser.
S22.03.where: Chat > answer made with web search > tap the 'Sources' pill under the answer

S22.08.needs: None beyond sign-in. The model must return a chart, so ask for one; the app has no button that makes a chart
S22.08.note: Charts come from a chart block in the answer (AssistantSurface.tsx 'chart' fence, or a mermaid xychart/pie block); whether the model returns one is not under the tester's control.
steps: Sign in and open the Chat screen.
Ask: 'Make a bar chart of monthly sales for January to June: 10, 14, 9, 17, 20, 12.'
When the chart appears in the answer, press and drag across the bars or line.
Look at the text line under the chart: it changes to show the value at that point.
For a pie chart, tap a slice to select it and tap again to clear. Compare with Expected: values show on touch and a legend-style readout appears.
S22.08.where: Chat > ask for a chart > the chart in the answer

S22.09.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a chart
S22.09.note: The code has no JSON view and no CSV download for chart data. 'Save image' exports a PNG.
steps: Get a chart in an answer, as in S22.08.
Tap 'Show data' under the chart. A table of the chart values appears.
Tap a value in the table and check it can be selected.
Tap 'Save image' and check a picture of the chart is saved or shared.
Compare the table values with the chart. Compare with Expected: the data is inspectable and can be saved.
S22.09.where: Chat > chart in an answer > 'Show data' button under the chart

labels.text: Map preview is unavailable. Place names are listed.

S22.10.needs: A managed Cloud account with map tiles available. This depends on production state and is not verified here
S22.10.note: The map appears only in Cloud mode and only when the answer has located places (a 'map' block). Whether production tiles are configured is not verified in code.
steps: Select 'Cloud' in the mode toggle on the Chat screen.
Ask: 'Show me the main museums in Paris on a map.'
Wait for the answer. A map with pins should appear under the text.
Tap the expand control on the map (its label is 'Full screen map').
Compare with Expected: the map shows markers. If the map cannot load, the text 'Map preview is unavailable. Place names are listed.' appears instead.
S22.10.where: Chat (Cloud mode) > ask about places > map in the answer > 'Full screen map' control

S22.28.needs: A Cloud account with a tool or connector that needs approval; the UI does not let the tester choose when it asks
S22.28.note: The card is CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx, shown in AgentActivityTimeline.tsx and ToolCallTimeline.tsx. The code does not show how often a tool asks for approval, so the trigger is unsure.
steps: Select 'Cloud' in the mode toggle and start a task that makes the agent use a tool needing approval.
When the agent pauses, find the approval card. Check it shows the tool summary and its parameters.
Read the buttons: 'Allow once', 'Allow for this chat', 'Always allow', 'Deny'.
Tap 'Deny' (or 'Allow once') and check the card shows the decision.
For 'Always allow' on a destructive tool, check a confirmation alert with 'Cancel' appears. Compare with Expected: the card states what will happen and offers approve or deny.
S22.28.where: Chat (Cloud mode) > a task where the agent asks to use a tool > approval card in the activity timeline with 'Allow once', 'Allow for this chat', 'Always allow', 'Deny'

S22.30.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a table
S22.30.note: A separate product comparison card exists (cards/ProductComparisonCard.tsx). Column headings sort only when the cell has no link.
steps: Ask: 'Compare three phone plans in a table: price, data, and contract length.'
Find the table in the answer and check its columns and rows read clearly.
Tap a column heading to sort the rows.
Tap the 'Expand table' icon to open the table full screen, then tap 'Close table'.
Compare with Expected: the answer shows a readable comparison table.
S22.30.where: Chat > ask for a comparison table > the table in the answer > 'Expand table'

S22.31.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a mermaid block
S22.31.note: No mind-map code exists by name. A mind map is drawn only as a generic mermaid block, and whether mindmap syntax renders is not verified in code.
steps: Ask: 'Draw a mind map of the parts of a bicycle as a mermaid mindmap.'
Wait for the answer. A 'Diagram' bar appears under the drawing.
Tap 'Show source' to see the diagram code, then tap 'Show source' again to hide it.
Tap the 'Expand diagram' icon to open it full screen.
Compare with Expected: a drawn mind map with a central topic and branches.
S22.31.where: Chat > ask for a mind map > the 'Diagram' bar under the drawing > 'Expand diagram' or 'Show source'

S22.32.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a mermaid block
S22.32.note: Flowcharts use the same generic mermaid path as mind maps; the code does not name flowcharts, so the drawing depends on the Mermaid runtime.
steps: Ask: 'Draw a flowchart of how a support ticket is handled, with decision points, as a mermaid flowchart.'
Wait for the answer. A 'Diagram' bar appears under the drawing.
Tap 'Show source' to see the diagram code, then hide it.
Tap the 'Expand diagram' icon to open it full screen.
Compare with Expected: a drawn flowchart with boxes and arrows.
S22.32.where: Chat > ask for a flowchart > the 'Diagram' bar under the drawing > 'Expand diagram' or 'Show source'

S22.33.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain a timeline block
S22.33.note: The timeline panel is the 'timeline' answer block (AssistantSurface.tsx). The panel is a list of steps, not a line drawing. A mermaid timeline block takes the generic diagram path instead.
steps: Ask: 'Make a timeline of the steps to launch a small app, with dates and status.'
Find the 'Timeline' panel in the answer.
Check the steps are numbered in order, each with a date when given.
Check each step's status label: 'Complete', 'In progress' or 'Not started'.
Compare with Expected: the answer shows a drawn timeline of the steps.
S22.33.where: Chat > ask for a timeline > the 'Timeline' panel in the answer (numbered steps with status labels)

S22.36.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must contain an html block
S22.36.note: HTML and React previews run scripts in a sandbox (SafeArtifactPreview.tsx). Links in the preview ask 'Open link?' first.
steps: Ask: 'Make a small interactive HTML demo with a button that counts clicks.'
When the html code block appears, tap 'Preview HTML'.
Tap the demo's button inside the preview and check the count changes.
Tap the 'Source' tab to see the code, then 'Preview' to go back.
Compare with Expected: the demo runs live inside the preview.
S22.36.where: Chat > ask for an interactive HTML page > html code card > 'Preview HTML'

S22.38.needs: None beyond sign-in; the answer must generate an app or page (the tester cannot force it)
S22.38.note: The publish path needs a published artifact; whether this account can publish is not verified in code.
steps: Ask: 'Build a small web page that shows a to-do list I can add items to.'
Tap the artifact card in the answer (it says 'Tap to expand').
In the full-screen view, check the 'Preview' tab shows the live page. Try adding an item.
Tap 'Source' and then 'Preview' again.
If the artifact has been published, find its publication link and 'Open in Safari' (iPhone) or 'Open in browser'. Compare with Expected: the app is previewed live and can be opened or expanded.
S22.38.where: Chat > ask for a small web app > artifact card in the answer > tap it > 'Preview' tab (and 'Open in Safari' when published)
